An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.

We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.

What you'll do

  • Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
  • Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
  • Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
  • Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
  • Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.
  • Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.
  • Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
  • Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.

What you'll bring

  • Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.
  • Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.
  • An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.
  • Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
  • The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.
  • Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

An overview of this role

As a Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you'll help build and maintain the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. You'll work alongside experienced engineers who guide the larger design decisions, delivering well-scoped changes and growing into ownership of larger parts of the system.

Today, that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every application programming interface (API) request. You'll work on fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and representational state transfer (REST) APIs that enforce them. A single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks, so correctness and performance both matter.

You'll also contribute to moving the permission model to a new authorization stack that pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine. The engine represents access relationships and evaluates permission rules, and can run within the monolith's process or be reached through remote procedure calls using gRPC. You don't need prior Rust experience: several engineers on the team learned it for this work, and we'll support you doing the same.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and the new authorization service
  • Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources, with guidance from senior engineers on the design

What you'll do

  • Implement authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith so permission checks allow intended access and deny unauthorized access.
  • Deliver well-scoped workstreams from feature-flagged rollout through verifying that the old and new systems produce the same results, with review and guidance from senior engineers.
  • Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles so additional resources have permission coverage consistent with the established catalog.
  • Extend and fix authorization enforcement so GraphQL and the REST API enforce the intended permissions consistently.
  • Make incremental refactors to long-lived policy code without changing behavior for existing customers.
  • Investigate and fix reliability, performance, and security issues so affected permission checks return the expected results without regressions.
  • Work with the authentication, platform, and artificial intelligence (AI) teams to document interface contracts that keep permission checks consistent as authorization moves toward a shared service.
  • Contribute to design documents, merge requests, and code reviews so proposed changes have a documented rationale and review feedback is addressed asynchronously.

What you'll bring

  • Solid experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, typically gained over 2 to 4 years or more.
  • Hands-on experience with authorization concepts, such as role-based access control or fine-grained permissions, from work or projects.
  • A security mindset: you treat a permission bug as a security bug and consider who a change could affect before choosing an implementation.
  • Experience making careful changes to existing codebases, including incremental refactors and feature-flagged rollouts that preserve existing behavior.
  • Familiarity with GraphQL or API authorization patterns.
  • Awareness of performance, including how repeated permission checks can add up on every request.
  • Strong written communication and the ability to work effectively when most decisions happen in a document or merge request rather than a meeting.
  • Helpful, but not required: hands-on PostgreSQL experience, or experience with Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture.

We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security.

About Commvault

Commvault (NASDAQ: CVLT) delivers continuous recovery for the AI era. We help organizations stay ready for constant disruption by returning critical data, applications, identities, and AI systems to a clean, trusted state. Our purpose-built recovery solutions span cloud-native and hybrid environments, leveraging AI to enable resilience at enterprise scale.

The Opportunity:

We have an exciting opportunity to join our Business Technology team. As we move toward an AI-driven delivery model, you will design and build end-to-end workflows that orchestrate ServiceNow, cloud platforms, enterprise systems, and AI agents into autonomous flows that resolve requests from intake through completion.

The ideal candidate starts with business outcomes and economics—understanding current costs and cycle times, defining target states, and designing the fastest path to achieve them. You will re-engineer processes before automating, determine what can be resolved autonomously versus requiring human intervention, and build the integrations that bring these solutions into production.

What you’ll do…

  • Orchestrate cross-platform workflows connecting ServiceNow, cloud services, identity systems, and enterprise applications to enable end-to-end request resolution without manual handoffs

  • Build AI-powered request resolution and autonomous operations (intent detection, diagnosis, and resolution), driving deflection before tickets are created

  • Integrate AI agents into workflows using MCP, tools, and orchestration patterns to pull context, take action, and escalate appropriately

  • Re-engineer processes before automating—eliminating unnecessary steps and designing improved workflows

  • Own automation economics and value realization, including measuring cost and cycle time, modeling improvements, and tracking business impact

  • Build and configure solutions on ServiceNow (Flow Designer, Integration Hub, scoped apps, catalog, Now Assist) alongside automation beyond the platform

  • Develop automation outside of ServiceNow using Python and PowerShell for cloud operations, identity management, monitoring, and scheduling

  • Design workflows that balance automation and human oversight—defining approval points, autonomy boundaries, and ensuring systems operate reliably and safely in production 

Who you are?

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field

  • 2–4 years of hands-on experience in software engineering, automation, or ServiceNow development, building production-grade solutions

  • Hands-on experience with ServiceNow development, including workflow automation (Flow Designer), integrations (REST/webhooks), and platform scripting

  • Experience working with authentication (OAuth, bearer tokens) and enterprise data models (e.g., CMDB)

  • Strong automation mindset with the ability to identify what should be orchestrated, automated, or eliminated

  • Solid engineering fundamentals (APIs, system design, data structures, scripting)

  • Experience with programming or scripting languages such as Python, Java, C#, or PowerShell

  • Experience building and integrating systems using REST APIs and enterprise platforms

  • Experience delivering end-to-end automation (design, build, deploy, monitor, measure)

  • Ability to work backward from business outcomes, with a focus on impact and efficiency

  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to operate in ambiguity and communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders

  • Demonstrated self-learning mindset in a rapidly evolving technology landscape

  • Curiosity to understand root causes—building solutions that address patterns, not just symptoms

  • Strong written and verbal English 

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Experience across additional ServiceNow modules (ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, CSM, SecOps, GRC)

  • Familiarity with ServiceNow capabilities such as Service Portal, UI Builder, Performance Analytics, Now Assist, or Virtual Agent

  • Experience building scoped applications (App Engine) and using automated testing frameworks (ATF)

  • Experience applying AI to workflow automation (e.g., request deflection, automated resolution, intent classification at scale)

  • Exposure to agent-based systems or orchestration patterns (e.g., MCP, tool integration, agent handoffs)

  • Familiarity with human-in-the-loop design, guardrails, and workflow governance

  • Experience with modern AI and integration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, RAG pipelines)

  • Familiarity with vector databases, observability tooling, monitoring, or process mining

  • Experience with integration platforms (e.g., Workato, MuleSoft)

  • ServiceNow certifications (CSA, CAD, CIS, or similar)

About the team

The Polaris Platform Bangalore team (a.k.a. Legion team) at Rubrik provides the core platforms and systems that enable product engineers to efficiently build and operate scalable and reliable applications in the cloud and also the on-prem version of the control plane. Polaris Platform has a horizontal charter with our customers being both external customers as well as Rubrik internal teams. Presently, the Legion team is working on enabling product led trials, license management & enforcement, making  its cloud deployment infrastructure more efficient. Legion team also owns the on-prem RSC (RSC-P) version and is currently working on supporting it on different deployments, while ensuring it scales and is performant like its cloud counterpart. 

About the role

We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our team. We believe in giving engineers responsibility, not tasks. Our goal is to motivate and challenge people to do their best work. To do that, we have a very fluid structure and give people flexibility to work on projects that they enjoy the most. This develops more capable engineers, and keeps everyone engaged and happy. To address challenges of huge year over year growth, our team is constantly re-imagining our platform. This is an exciting time to join as we are constantly improving and innovating on each of our core layers.

Some recent projects include:

  • Enabling product assisted trials to decrease sales cycles
  • Bringing in Licensing visibility and enforcement for customers
  • Scaling our single node on-prem control plane (RSC-P) to multi node
  • Bringing in deployment efficiency to improve developer productivity

What you’ll do

  • Build our platforms, systems and infrastructure using your strong background in distributed systems and large scale storage systems.
  • Design, develop, test, deploy, maintain and improve the software.

  • Rubrik Software Engineers are self-starters, driven, and can manage themselves. Bottom line, if you have a limitless drive and like to win, we want to talk to you - come make history!

jobs.role: Database Reliability Engineer/Database Engineer (Rubrik Security Cloud Platform)
jobs.description:
About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Database Reliability Engineer to own the reliability, performance, and scalability of our end-to-end database infrastructure. You will manage both our low-latency transactional engines and our real-time analytical/lakehouse storage systems. You will bridge systems engineering, database internals, and automation to maintain rock-solid data integrity, low query latency, and high availability across the entire data lifecycle.

What you'll do

  • Performance & Query Optimization: Diagnose and resolve latency regressions, lock/latch contention, index strategies, and memory/disk bottlenecks across both row-oriented and columnar engines.
  • Disaster Recovery & Data Integrity: Ensure strict RTO/RPO adherence, automated backup validation, PITR (point-in-time recovery), and data consistency across transactional and analytical stores.
  • Storage Optimization & Compaction: Manage compaction policies, partition strategies, file sizing, and storage tiering to minimize storage costs and read amplification.
  • Transactional Reliability & Operations: Manage HA, automated failover, replication topology, and zero-downtime maintenance for production RDBMS clusters.
  • Analytical Storage Infrastructure: Maintain, scale, and optimize real-time analytical engines (ClickHouse) and lakehouse formats/engines (Apache Iceberg, BigQuery).
  • Infrastructure as Code & Observability: Build declarative automation for cluster provisioning, schema migrations, and metric alerting (Prometheus, PromQL, Grafana)

Experience you'll need

  • Database Internals & RDBMS Fundamentals:
    • Deep understanding of ACID guarantees, WAL, checkpointing, and recovery mechanics (e.g., ARIES-style recovery).
    • Comprehensive grasp of concurrency control, transaction isolation levels, lock protocols (2PL, deadlocks), and MVCC architectures.
    • Deep knowledge of storage structures: B+ Trees, LSM-Trees, and columnar storage layouts (e.g., Parquet, ORC, ClickHouse Wide/Compact formats).
  • Operational Database Experience:
    • 4+ years running production database infrastructure, with deep expertise in [PostgreSQL / MySQL].
    • Experience optimizing and managing cost/quotas in Google Cloud BigQuery (partitioning, clustering, reservation slots).
    • Experience with OLAP DB like: ClickHouse, BQ
  • Systems & Kernel Engineering:
    • Strong Linux fundamentals: I/O subsystems, page cache vs. engine buffer pools, disk alignment, asynchronous I/O, and memory management.
    • Automation & Software Engineering:
    • Using  Python or Go for building database automation, operators, and CLI tooling.
    • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and container orchestration.

Preferred skills and qualifications

  • Hands-on administration and performance tuning of ClickHouse (cluster topologies, ZooKeeper/Keeper coordination, MergeTree engine family, mutations, and compaction).
  • Experience with change data capture (CDC) pipelines (e.g., Debezium, Kafka) feeding transactional updates into ClickHouse/Iceberg.
  • Experience managing lakehouse storage patterns using Apache Iceberg (metadata management, snapshot expiration, file compaction/orphan cleanup).
  • Experience with automated schema migration tools (e.g., gh-ost, Liquibase, Bytebase).
  • Familiarity with distributed consensus engines ( ClickHouse Keeper,Raft, Paxos).
